title: The India Pit Stop pulls into Singapore
summary: Cashfree brought the India Pit Stop to Singapore during Singapore Fintech Festival, connecting global fintechs, banks and payment leaders for conversations on India's payments ecosystem.
body_markdown:
Table of Contents


Toggle


Singapore Fintech Festival is one of the busiest weeks of the year in payments. The halls at Singapore EXPO fill up, calendars fill up faster, and most conversations happen standing up between sessions.


On the evening of 19 November, we tried something different. We invited a small group of leaders from global fintechs, banks, payment platforms and businesses to Mandala Club, gave them a comfortable chair and a drink, and talked about cross-border payments, India’s fintech ecosystem and everything in between.


##


**Where the idea came from**


The India Pit Stop started in Mumbai. At Global Fintech Fest in September, we hosted the first one at Arts Cafe: an invite-only evening with no presentations and no agenda. It led to some of our best conversations of the week, so we decided to take it on the road.


Singapore was the natural next stop. Many global platforms run their Asia plans from here, and India is often part of those plans. So this time, we brought the conversation to them.


##


**Conversations, not decks**


Mandala Club sits in a restored shophouse in Tanjong Pagar, well away from the expo halls. Guests came in from six o’clock, some for an hour between commitments, some for the whole evening.


There were no slides and nobody on stage. People moved between the lounge chairs and the bar over small plates and drinks, and the Cashfree team, who have spent ten years building payments in India, spent the evening talking with them. On the way out, guests picked up a small gift from our Cross-Border Payments team.


##


**Who was in the room**


The room brought together payment platforms, fintechs, banks and advisors who are shaping cross-border payments, each with India somewhere in their plans. Guests came from Ant, Boku, DRX, EBANX, EximPe, Flutterwave, Forter, Gradient, Identity, J.P. Morgan, PwC, Silence, Standard Chartered, Stripe and Worldpay.


##


**What we heard**


With no slides to get through, the talk turned quickly to the practical side of doing business in India. Four topics kept coming back.


- **The licensing question has moved on.** RBI’s PA-CB rules for cross-border payment aggregators have been in place since 2023, and final licences have been granted. For global platforms, the decision today is which licensed partner can get them live in India fastest.
- **UPI is going global.** Indian buyers pay with UPI at home, and it increasingly works across borders too, including through the UPI–PayNow link here in Singapore. For a global platform, accepting UPI means reaching Indian customers wherever they are.
- **Recurring payments work differently.** RBI’s e-mandate rules require customers to approve payments above set limits, so the card-on-file model used in the US and Europe doesn’t carry over neatly. Subscription businesses need to plan for this early.
- **India runs on partnerships.** No single player covers a cross-border payment into India end to end. Global payment companies, locally licensed aggregators, AD-1 banks that handle settlement, and fraud and identity providers each own a piece. The more of those pieces work together, the easier India gets for everyone.


##


**Next stop**


Mumbai, then Singapore. We plan to take the Pit Stop to more cities around the world, and the idea will stay the same: the easiest way to understand India is to sit down with people who build there.


If you are planning your move in India and would like an invite to the next one, write to us atxb-sales@cashfree.com .
